title: A degree-p presentation with a unit derivation
statement: Let A be a complete Noetherian local domain with fraction field K, and C a complete Noetherian local A-algebra with local structure map, formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let L/K be finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], with K of prime characteristic p, and M an intermediate field with [L:M] = p. Give M and L their compatible A-algebra structures. Then for R = M tensor_A C [def-weil-module-base-change], there exist f in R, a Z-derivation D of R with D(f) a unit, and a ring isomorphism R[z]/(z^p-f) to L tensor_A C. No regularity hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PM, proof of (4) => (1), coefficient reduction and final two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07PM

proof.text: Work directly over the specified field M. Choose x outside M in L and let r be the least exponent for which x^(p^r) lies in M. The previous power beta has beta^p = g in M and beta outside M. Frobenius injectivity shows g is not a pth power. Mathlib X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime and minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic identify the minimal polynomial. IntermediateField.isSimpleOrder_of_finrank_prime, applied to [L:M] = p, makes M(beta) = L. minpoly.equivAdjoin therefore gives M[X]/(X^p-g) equiv L. This is the proved private helper degree_p_coefficient; the full pth-root tower is unnecessary.

Construct a finite A-subalgebra B of M explicitly as the adjoin of an integral K-basis provided by Mathlib FiniteDimensional.exists_is_basis_integral (its proof scales a basis by a common nonzero denominator). Algebra.finite_adjoin_of_finite_of_isIntegral makes B finite over A. For each z in M, clear the finite family of basis coordinates using IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite. The basis expansion gives d*z in B for a nonzero d in A, so every z is a quotient of two elements of B. Verify all three IsFractionRing fields directly. Write g = c/e in this fraction field and put f0 = e^(p-1)*c in B. Then f0 maps to e^p*g. If f0 had a pth root x in M, x/e would be a pth root of g. No data is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

The algebra B is a domain of characteristic p, finite type over the complete Noetherian local A, with fraction field M. Apply Derivation.exists_apply_ne_zero_of_not_pth_power to f0 to obtain an absolute derivation D0 of B with D0(f0) nonzero.

Set T = C tensor_A B with the right B-algebra structure and n the extended maximal ideal of C. Base change makes T formally smooth over B for n. The tensor is finite over C, so finite_module_complete_over_complete_noetherian makes it complete as a C-module; IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff gives completeness for n. Apply Derivation.exists_extension_of_formallySmoothAdic to obtain DT agreeing with D0 on B.

Set W to the images of the nonzero elements of B in T, and U = T tensor_B M. IsLocalization.tensor makes U a localization at W. Use the already proved upstream IsLocalization.extendDerivation with the identity ring map and the additive map obtained by composing DT with T -> U; Derivation.mk' packages the extension as an integer derivation. Tensor commutation, commRight, and cancelBaseChange identify U with M tensor_A C. Conjugate the derivation through this ring equivalence and verify its values on every b in B. In particular D(f0) is the image of D0(f0), hence a unit. The image of p in the tensor is zero even if the tensor ring is trivial; the Leibniz power rule gives D(e^p)=0. Since f0=e^p*g, D(f0)=e^p*D(g). A factor of a unit product is a unit, so D(g) is a unit. These constructions are proved private helpers, not new assumed statements.

Keep the original coefficient g in the final presentation. Build Polynomial M tensor_A C equiv Polynomial (M tensor_A C) explicitly using cancelBaseChange, tensor commutation, the unique-variable polynomial equivalence and MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv. Check that the relation X^p-C(g) maps to X^p-C(g tensor 1). Ideal.map_span and Ideal.quotientEquiv transport the principal ideal. Algebra.TensorProduct.quotientTensorEquiv and TensorProduct.congr applied to the field presentation finish the ring equivalence. Combine this equivalence with the derivation and its unit value. The proof uses no regularity or nontriviality of the generic fibre.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07PM, final two paragraphs; fixed-intermediate-field presentation and explicit tensor transport by N3, using the integral basis construction in Mathlib.

theorem exists_degree_p_presentation_unit_derivation_of_formallySmoothAdic
    (A : Type u) (C : Type v) (K : Type u) (L : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [CommRing C] [IsLocalRing C] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra A C] [Algebra A K] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L]
    [IsScalarTower A K L] [IsFractionRing A K] [Module.Finite K L]
    [IsPurelyInseparable K L]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A C)]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C) C]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p]
    (M : IntermediateField K L) [Algebra A M] [IsScalarTower A K M]
    (hdegree : Module.finrank M L = p)
    (hfs : FormallySmoothAdic A C (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C)) :
    ∃ (f : TensorProduct A M C) (D : Derivation ℤ (TensorProduct A M C)
      (TensorProduct A M C)), IsUnit (D f) ∧
      Nonempty ((Polynomial (TensorProduct A M C) ⧸
        Ideal.span {Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C f}) ≃+* TensorProduct A L C)
